title: Unit-normalized reflection of coefficient squares and their adjunction mates
statement:
For $i=0,1$ let $\mathcal A_i,\mathcal B_i$ be categories, each with a full reflective subcategory of local objects. Write $\Lambda_{i,T}$ for the reflector followed by inclusion and $\eta_{i,T}:\operatorname{id}\to\Lambda_{i,T}$ for its unit, with $T=A,B$. Thus $\Lambda_{i,T}M$ is local and precomposition with $\eta_M$ bijects maps to every local object. Let $F_i:\mathcal A_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal B_i:G_i$ be specified adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume $G_i$ sends local objects to local objects and is equipped with a natural isomorphism $\gamma_i:\Lambda_{i,A}G_i\xrightarrow{\sim}G_i\Lambda_{i,B}$ satisfying $\gamma_{i,M}\eta_{i,A,G_iM}=G_i(\eta_{i,B,M})$.

Let $C_A:\mathcal A_0\to\mathcal A_1$, $C_B:\mathcal B_0\to\mathcal B_1$ have natural isomorphisms $\kappa_T:C_T\Lambda_{0,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{1,T}C_T$ satisfying $\kappa_{T,M}C_T(\eta_{0,T,M})=\eta_{1,T,C_TM}$. Let $\delta:F_1C_A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_BF_0$, and let $\beta:C_AG_0\to G_1C_B$ be its right mate for the specified adjunctions.

Then $\widehat F_i=\Lambda_{i,B}F_i$ on local inputs is left adjoint to the restriction $\widehat G_i$ of $G_i$, with Hom bijection obtained by precomposing with the reflection unit and then taking the original adjunct. The $C_T$ preserve local objects. On local inputs the induced comparison
$$\widehat\delta=\kappa_B^{-1}\circ\Lambda_{1,B}(\delta):\widehat F_1C_A\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B\widehat F_0$$
has right mate precisely the restriction of $\beta$. On every ambient $M\in\mathcal B_0$ one has the normalization equation
$$\beta_{\Lambda_{0,B}M}\,C_A(\gamma_{0,M})=G_1(\kappa_{B,M}^{-1})\,\gamma_{1,C_BM}\,\Lambda_{1,A}(\beta_M)\,\kappa_{A,G_0M}.$$
For composable diagrams with these data, pasting coefficient squares or pasting adjunctions before this construction gives the same comparisons as pasting afterwards, using the composition comparisons determined by the displayed Hom bijections. Identity squares give the identity comparisons. If the categories have shifts and all the specified functors, units, $\gamma$, $\kappa$ and $\delta$ respect them, these conclusions respect shifts as well. No invertibility of $\beta$ is assumed.
